description: How verified provider claims become auth_context. Every SDK adapter is emitted from this table (sdks/tools/generate_auth_adapters.py) and must produce the exact JSON in auth-context-vectors.json. A claim that is missing, of the wrong type, out of range or fails its kind maps to absent, never to a stronger assurance; only issuer and subject are required, and an adapter refuses to build a context without them.

rules.claims: A claim path is a list of keys. A key that is not an object at that depth makes the claim absent. No listed claim name contains a dot.
rules.id: The first claim whose value is a string that matches its kind. Anything else is skipped.
rules.list: Items come from an array of strings or from one string split by `split`. Items that do not match the kind are dropped, the list is cut at `max`, and the first claim that yields at least one item wins. A claim of any other type is skipped.
rules.time: A number in 0 to 253402300799 (a NumericDate) becomes RFC 3339 UTC in whole seconds, the fraction truncated. A string is kept only when it matches the time kind (RFC 3339 with an upper-case T and Z). Anything else is absent.
rules.bool: Only a JSON boolean counts; the strings "true" and "false" are skipped.
rules.actor: True when the claim is an object with a non-empty string `sub` or `email` (RFC 8693 act), or a non-empty string. Any other value, including an empty object, is false. The result is always sent, false included.
rules.mfa_factor_age: claim[index] must be a JSON number from 0 to `maxSeconds` / `unitSeconds`; the context gets mfa {present: true, age_seconds: trunc(value * unitSeconds)}. A negative value (Clerk -1 is no second factor), a non-number, a missing index or an out-of-range value gives no mfa.
rules.mfa_methods: The claim must be an array. Strings that match the kind are kept, up to `max`. present is true when any kept value equals `mfaValue` ignoring case; methods lists the kept values except those equal to an `ignore` value ignoring case. No methods gives no mfa, so a password-only amr sends nothing.
rules.mfa_aal: `claim` must be a string in `absent` (mfa {present: false}) or in `present` (mfa {present: true}); any other value gives no mfa. Only for `present`, the `amr` claim is read: an array whose items are a string or an object with a string `methodKey`; each name found in `factors` adds its mapped name once, in array order. No such name sends present alone. A name outside `factors` (a first factor, a refresh marker) is never listed.
rules.mfa_factor: The claim must be a string that matches the kind; the context gets mfa {present: true, methods: [value]}. Anything else gives no mfa.
rules.marker: Sends `value` when any `when` entry matches: the claim's JSON value has the same type and value as `equals` (the boolean true does not match the string "true" or the number 1). Used only for a downgrade: an anonymous user is sent as assurance_level low, and no claim ever sends a higher level.
rules.overrides: A key in overrides replaces the mapped value, false and empty included. A null override is ignored. Overrides are written by the caller from verified records and are not filtered.
rules.audience: audience defaults to the first mapped audience, or to the first item of an audiences override, when the context has audiences and no audience override.
rules.split: `whitespace` splits on runs of space, tab, CR, LF, FF and VT; `comma_whitespace` also splits on commas; `none` keeps a string whole. Empty pieces never match a kind.

workos.notes: AuthKit access token: org_id, role, permissions, sid; act holds the impersonator. aud is read as for any OIDC token; client_id is not an audience. Contact verification comes from the user record via overrides.

clerk.notes: Session token v2 puts the organization in o {id, rol, per} and factor ages in fva [first, second] minutes; v1 used org_id, org_role and org_permissions. iat is a 60-second refresh clock, so it is never sent as issued_at; session age is the session_created_at override. act marks impersonation.

auth0.notes: ID token, userinfo or normalised session claims; not an opaque access token. amr lists methods, and only the value mfa proves a second factor. org_id is set when an organization signed in. Contact verification is read from email_verified and phone_number_verified only.

supabase.notes: Supabase Auth access token, verified with the project's legacy HS256 secret or its published JWKS. aal is aal1 or aal2, and aal2 means a second factor. amr is [{method, timestamp}], newest first; the second-factor methods are the ones supabase/auth counts toward aal2, and the slash in their names becomes a colon to fit the method kind. is_anonymous and app_metadata.provider anonymous mark an anonymous sign-in. session_id is the session; sid and auth_time are not read. role is the Postgres role. email, phone and user_metadata are not read: contact verification and account age come from the user record via overrides, and factor age from the amr timestamps.

firebase.notes: Firebase ID token, verified with the Admin SDK verifyIdToken. Custom claims sit at the top level beside the Firebase claims, so only the reserved names are read: iss, sub, aud, iat, exp, auth_time and the firebase object. sid, roles, scopes, organisation and email_verified are never read, because a custom claim can carry those names. firebase.sign_in_second_factor (phone or totp) proves a second factor, firebase.tenant is the Identity Platform tenant, and firebase.sign_in_provider anonymous marks an anonymous user. Contact verification and account age come from the Admin SDK user record via overrides.

oidc.notes: Any other provider: base claims only, under a lowercase slug the customer chooses. Every other fact comes from overrides.
